extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for object detection and segmentation containing 328,000 images with 2.5 million labeled instances across 91 object categories. The dataset focuses on detecting objects in complex everyday scenes in their natural context, with per-instance segmentations for precise object localization.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: T. Lin, M. Maire, S. Belongie, J. Hays, P. Perona, D. Ramanan, P. Dollár, and C. L. Zitnick, "Microsoft COCO: Common objects in context," in ECCV, 2014.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr using pairwise combinations of object categories (e.g., 'dog + car') and scene/object category pairs to find non-iconic images containing multiple objects in natural contexts. At most 5 photos taken by a single photographer within a short time window were downloaded. A total of 328,000 images were collected.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were harvested from Flickr, a photo-sharing platform containing photos uploaded by amateur photographers with searchable metadata and keywords. Images were retrieved using queries for pairs of objects in conjunction with scene-based queries.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed using detection methods. Images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize the chance of near-duplicate images existing across train/validation/test splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An AMT filtering task was used to remove invalid or iconic images from candidate images. Workers were shown grids of 128 candidates and asked to remove iconic images. Instructions included examples of iconic and non-iconic images to guide workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation pipeline: (1) Category labeling - workers indicated which object categories were present by dragging category icons onto instances; (2) Instance spotting - workers placed crosses on all instances (up to 10) of each category; (3) Instance segmentation - workers segmented each object instance using a modified interface from OpenSurfaces project. For images with more than 10 instances of a category, remaining instances were marked as 'crowds' using a single segment. All workers completed a training task for each object category before being allowed to segment instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). Modified user interface from OpenSurfaces project for segmentation tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multiple workers (3 to 5) judged each segmentation to ensure quality. Segmentations of insufficient quality were discarded and instances added back to the pool. Workers who consistently produced poor segmentations had all their work discarded. Segmentations required at least 4 of 5 favorable votes to be accepted.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Category labeling: 8 workers per image. Instance spotting: 8 workers per image. Instance segmentation: 1 worker per instance. Segmentation verification: 3-5 workers per segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is split into two roughly equal parts. The first half (2014 release) contains 82,783 training, 40,504 validation, and 40,775 testing images. The cumulative 2015 release will contain a total of 165,482 train, 81,208 val, and 81,434 test images. Annotations for train and validation data are released, but not for test. The 2014 release is limited to a subset of 80 categories out of 91 total categories.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset was designed to reduce iconic image bias by collecting non-iconic images showing objects in natural contexts, partially occluded, amid clutter, and in non-canonical perspectives. However, some categories rarely co-occurred with others, requiring single-category searches with explicit filtering to remove iconic images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only labels 'thing' categories (objects with clear boundaries) and not 'stuff' categories (materials and objects with no clear boundaries like sky, street, grass). The dataset is limited to entry-level categories rather than fine-grained categories. Some object categories may be parts of other object categories. The 2014 release omitted 11 categories due to various issues: hat, shoe, eyeglasses (too many instances), mirror, window, door, street sign (ambiguous and difficult to label), plate, desk (confusion with bowl and dining table), blender, hair brush (too few instances).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is designed for object detection and segmentation tasks, advancing scene understanding including recognizing objects, localizing objects in 2D, and providing precise 2D localization of objects. The dataset enables learning detailed object models capable of precise 2D localization and contextual reasoning between objects.
